title: Invariant powers in a reduced normal field tensor product
statement: Let $K$ be a field, let $L/K$ be any field extension, and let $E/K$ be a finite-dimensional normal field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. Here normal means that the minimal polynomial over $K$ of each element of $E$ splits into linear factors in $E[T]$. Give $T=L\otimes_KE$ its commutative algebra multiplication $(l\otimes e)(l^{\prime}\otimes e^{\prime})=ll^{\prime}\otimes ee^{\prime}$ [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], and put $R=T/\sqrt{(0)}$, where $\sqrt{(0)}$ is the ideal of nilpotent elements. The map $L\to R$ is $l\mapsto\overline{l\otimes1}$. The group $G=\operatorname{Aut}_K(E)$ acts by $\sigma(\overline{l\otimes e})=\overline{l\otimes\sigma(e)}$. For every $x\in R$ fixed by all $\sigma\in G$, there are an integer $N\geq1$ and $l\in L$ with $x^N=\overline{l\otimes1}$. If $\operatorname{char}K=0$, one can take $N=1$; if $\operatorname{char}K=p>0$, one can take $N=p^r$ for some integer $r\geq0$. Neither separability of $E/K$ nor any finiteness assumption on $L/K$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09EU, lemma-galois-relative, proof: invariant elements in the reduced tensor algebra; corrected invariant-power formulation for normal extensions that may be inseparable.

proof.text: Finite dimension makes $E/K$ algebraic: the powers of each element are linearly dependent over $K$. Put $S=E^G$. By [lem-weil-pbc-normal-extension-purely-inseparable-then-galois], $S$ is an intermediate field, $S/K$ is purely inseparable and $E/S$ is separable and normal. A finite $K$-spanning set of $E$ also spans over $S$, so $E/S$ is finite. Every $K$-automorphism fixes $S$ by its definition, and every $S$-automorphism fixes $K$; hence $G=\operatorname{Aut}_S(E)$, which is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field]. In characteristic zero $S=K$ by [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension].

Write $\pi:T\to R$ for the quotient. The maps $l\otimes e\mapsto l\otimes\sigma(e)$ are mutually inverse ring automorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]; they preserve nilpotents, so $\pi$ is equivariant for the stated action. Choose $t\in T$ with $\pi(t)=x$. In characteristic zero, step 1 makes $E/K$ finite separable. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-tensor-field-reduced], with the tensor factors interchanged, $T$ is reduced, so $\pi$ is injective. Thus $t$ is fixed by $G$; put $y=t$ and $q=1$. In characteristic $p>0$, for each $\sigma\in G$ the difference $d_\sigma=\sigma(t)-t$ is nilpotent because $\pi(d_\sigma)=0$. Choose $n_\sigma\geq1$ with $d_\sigma^{n_\sigma}=0$. Finiteness of $G$ gives $a\geq0$ with $p^a\geq n_\sigma$ for all $\sigma$. By [def-weil-ring-frobenius], $\sigma(t^{p^a})-t^{p^a}=d_\sigma^{p^a}=0$. Put $q=p^a$ and $y=t^q$. In either case $y\in T^G$ and $\pi(y)=x^q$.

source.place: Tag 09EU, lemma-galois-relative, proof: lift a reduced invariant and raise to a power. Reducedness in characteristic zero uses Algebra Tag 030U, lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness; Frobenius is the ring calculation after Varieties Tag 03SM.

proof.text: Choose a $K$-basis $(b_i)$ of $L$ by [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-basis-through-vector]. By [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension], $(b_i\otimes1)$ is an $E$-basis of $T=L\otimes_KE$. Write $y=\sum_{i\in I}b_i\otimes e_i$ with $I$ finite. The action sends this sum to $\sum_{i\in I}b_i\otimes\sigma(e_i)$. Since $y$ is fixed, uniqueness of basis coordinates gives $\sigma(e_i)=e_i$ for every $\sigma$, so each $e_i\in S$. This uses no finiteness of $L/K$.

source.place: Tag 09EU, lemma-galois-relative, proof: the fixed-tensor calculation; basis-coordinate details supplied by Q94. Compare Varieties Tag 038B, lemma-closed-fixed-by-Galois, invariant coefficients.

proof.text: In characteristic zero $S=K$, so the sum in step 3 equals $l\otimes1$ with $l=\sum_{i\in I}b_i e_i\in L$, by tensor balancing. As $q=1$, applying $\pi$ gives $x=\overline{l\otimes1}$, as required with $N=1$. In characteristic $p>0$, by [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] choose $r_i\geq0$ with $e_i^{p^{r_i}}\in K$. Take $b=\max(\{r_i:i\in I\}\cup\{0\})$, so every $e_i^{p^b}\in K$. Frobenius and the tensor multiplication of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] give, using [def-weil-ring-frobenius], $y^{p^b}=\sum_{i\in I}b_i^{p^b}\otimes e_i^{p^b}=l\otimes1$, where $l=\sum_{i\in I}b_i^{p^b}e_i^{p^b}\in L$. Apply $\pi$ and use $q=p^a$ to obtain $x^{p^{a+b}}=\overline{l\otimes1}$. The exponent $N=p^{a+b}$ is positive. The empty sum gives $l=0$ and $b=0$.
